new_page.title: Property Transfer Tax on a New Home in BC: Newly Built Exemption
new_page.h1: Is there property transfer tax on a new home in BC?
new_page.description: A newly built home you will live in is exempt from BC property transfer tax up to $1,100,000, with a partial exemption up to $1,150,000. How it works.

breadcrumbs.name: Is there property transfer tax on a new home in BC?

faq.q: Do I have to be a first-time buyer for the new home exemption?
faq.a: No. Any buyer who will live in the newly built home as their principal residence can qualify, if they meet the other requirements.

faq.q: Does it apply to a presale assignment?
faq.a: Ask your lawyer or notary before you sign. An assignment changes who registers the home and when, which affects both this exemption and the home flipping tax.

parts.t: Usually not, if it will be your home. Since April 1, 2024 the newly built home exemption removes property transfer tax entirely on a new home with a fair market value up to $1,100,000, and partly up to $1,150,000. You do not have to be a first-time buyer.
Between $1,100,000 and $1,150,000 the exemption shrinks in a straight line to zero. If only one of two buyers qualifies, the exemption covers that buyer's share.

The home must be newly built and used as your principal residence. Presale condos and townhomes bought from the builder are the common case in Surrey, Langley and South Surrey. Land over half a hectare (about 1.24 acres) is worked out differently: only the home and a share of the land count.
New homes carry 5% GST. First-time buyers can get up to $50,000 of it back on a new home under $1 million, with a partial rebate up to $1.5 million.
Read on November 18, 2026. Rules change, so confirm with the source or your lawyer, notary or accountant before you act.
